sources.title: Art. 30 GDPR – Records of processing activities
sources.key_facts: Controller RoPA required fields (Art.30.1): name_and_contact_details, purposes, data_subject_categories, personal_data_categories, recipient_categories, third_country_transfers, retention_periods, security_measures. Processor RoPA: name_and_contact_details, categories_of_processing, third_country_transfers, security_measures. Art.30(3): must be in writing including electronic form. Art.30(5): exemption for organizations < 250 employees unless processing is high-risk, non-occasional, or involves special categories.

sources.title: Art. 83 GDPR – General conditions for imposing administrative fines
sources.key_facts: Tier 1 (Art.83.4): up to EUR 10,000,000 or 2% of total worldwide annual turnover (whichever is higher). Applies to Arts. 8, 11, 25-39, 42-43. Tier 2 (Art.83.5): up to EUR 20,000,000 or 4% of total worldwide annual turnover (whichever is higher). Applies to Arts. 5-7, 9, 12-22, 44-49, member state laws Ch.IX, non-compliance with Art.58 supervisory authority orders. Art.83(2) lists 11 factors for fine calculation including nature, gravity, duration, intentionality, mitigation, prior violations, cooperation, data categories.

sources.title: Art. 33 GDPR – Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
sources.key_facts: Art.33(1): 72-hour deadline after becoming aware. Exception: not required if breach is unlikely to result in risk to rights and freedoms. Art.33(3) required fields: (a) nature_of_breach including categories and approximate number of data subjects and records, (b) DPO_contact name and details, (c) likely_consequences, (d) measures_taken or proposed including mitigation. Art.33(4): phased reporting allowed. Art.33(5): controller must document all breaches. Processor must notify controller without undue delay.

sources.title: Art. 12 GDPR – Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject
sources.key_facts: Art.12(3): Response to data subject requests (Arts. 15-22) must be provided within 1 month of receipt. Extension of up to 2 further months allowed for complex/numerous requests, but requester must be informed within initial 1 month with reasons. Responses must be free of charge (except manifestly unfounded/excessive requests). Art.12(4): If refusing, notify within 1 month with reasons. Communication must be concise, transparent, intelligible, easily accessible, in clear plain language.

sources.title: Art. 15 GDPR – Right of access by the data subject
sources.key_facts: Art.15(1): Data subject can obtain confirmation of processing and access to personal data. Must provide: processing purposes, categories of personal data, recipients/recipient categories, storage duration or criteria, rights to rectification/erasure/restriction, complaint rights with supervisory authorities, data source if not collected from subject, automated decision-making details. Art.15(3): 'The controller shall provide a copy of the personal data undergoing processing.' Additional copies may incur reasonable administrative fee.

sources.title: Art. 37 GDPR – Designation of the data protection officer
sources.key_facts: Art.37(1) three mandatory DPO appointment cases: (a) processing by public authority or body (except courts in judicial capacity), (b) core activities require regular and systematic monitoring of data subjects on large scale, (c) core activities consist of large-scale processing of special categories (Art.9) or criminal conviction data (Art.10). Art.37(5): DPO must be designated based on professional qualities including expert knowledge of data protection law and practices. Art.37(6): DPO can be employee or external contractor. Art.37(7): contact details must be published and communicated to supervisory authority.

sources.title: Art. 5 GDPR – Principles relating to processing of personal data
sources.key_facts: Art.5(1) six principles: (a) lawfulness_fairness_transparency, (b) purpose_limitation, (c) data_minimisation, (d) accuracy, (e) storage_limitation, (f) integrity_and_confidentiality. Art.5(2) accountability: 'The controller shall be responsible for, and be able to demonstrate compliance with' the six principles. Violations of Art.5 fall under Tier 2 fines (up to EUR 20M or 4% turnover).

sources.title: Art. 35 GDPR – Data protection impact assessment
sources.key_facts: Art.35(1): DPIA required prior to processing when likely to result in high risk. Art.35(3) mandatory triggers: (a) systematic and extensive profiling with significant effects including automated decision-making, (b) large-scale processing of special categories (Art.9) or criminal conviction data (Art.10), (c) systematic monitoring of publicly accessible areas on large scale. EDPB guidelines: if processing meets 2 or more of 9 risk criteria, DPIA generally required. Nine criteria: evaluation/scoring, automated decision-making with legal effect, systematic monitoring, sensitive data, large-scale, data set matching/combining, vulnerable subjects, innovative technology use, preventing exercise of right.

sources.title: CIRCL Compliance GitHub – GDPR Art.30 Processing Activities Records JSON Schema
sources.key_facts: Top-level schema fields: id, name, purpose (enum), description (object), legal_ground (object), data_subjects (array), personal_data (object with source array and data array), retention_period (string), controller, joint_controllers (array), data_processor, recipients (array), international_transfer (object with transfer boolean and entity_list), data_subject_rights (object with right_of_access, right_of_rectification, right_of_erasure, right_of_restriction, right_to_data_portability, right_to_object, automation_profiling), security_measures (object with pseudonymisation and others array). References GDPR Art.30(1)(e).

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines 9/2022 on personal data breach notification under GDPR (Version 2.0)
sources.key_facts: Published: 4 April 2023 (final). Key update in v2.0: paragraph 73 concerning notification requirements for personal data breaches at non-EU establishments. Controllers must document all breaches per Art.33(5) even if not notified to SA. Risk assessment must consider: nature and sensitivity of data, ease of identification of individuals, severity of consequences, category and number of data subjects impacted. Phased reporting recognized when full details unavailable within 72 hours. Total fines tracked: EUR 6.28B across 3,183 enforcement actions (as of Enforcement Tracker).

sources.title: EUR-Lex – Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) Full Text, CELEX:32016R0679
sources.key_facts: Official consolidated GDPR text. Recital 82: controllers and processors must maintain records of processing activities. Recital 85: breach notification to supervisory authority 'without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours'. Recitals 84, 90-94 cover DPIA requirements for high-risk processing. Full legal basis for all GDPR compliance obligations.

sources.title: GDPR Enforcement Tracker – CMS Law Fines Database
sources.key_facts: 3,183 tracked enforcement actions as of 2026. Total fines: EUR 6.28B. Notable cases: Meta EUR 1.2B (Irish DPC, May 2023, Art.46 transfer), TikTok EUR 345M (Irish DPC, Sep 2023, child data), LinkedIn EUR 310M (Irish DPC, Oct 2024, consent/legal basis), Uber EUR 290M (Dutch DPA, 2024, international transfer), Clearview AI EUR 30.5M (Dutch DPA, Sep 2024, biometric data). Amazon France EUR 32M (CNIL, Dec 2023, Art.88 employee monitoring).
